svg.title: Cell biology overview
svg.desc: Six clearly divided sections explain cell structures, specialised cells, microscopy, division and stem cells, culturing, and transport with exchange. Mitosis is the only diagram. Bold labels with colons introduce explanations. A complete text counterpart is also available.

g.text: Nucleus: stores DNA and controls the cell.
Membrane: controls what enters and leaves.
No nucleus: main DNA is a circular loop.
Much smaller than animal and plant cells.
Some have small DNA rings called plasmids.
Sperm: the tail helps it swim.
Nerve: a long axon carries impulses.
Muscle: contracts to move the body.
Root hair: large area for absorption.
Takes in water and mineral ions.
Most animal cells do this early in life.
Many plant cells can do this for life.
Resolution: tell two close points apart.
Use the same units for both sizes.
Same chromosome number as the parent.
Stem cells: unspecialised, able to divide.
Bone marrow: some types, including blood.
Net particle movement from high to low
No energy from respiration is needed.
Water moves from a dilute solution
to a concentrated solution through a
Large area and thin barrier aid diffusion.
Large organisms have a lower SA/V.
